title: Provider records are validated at boot; the state machine reasons against fields, not vendor names
asA: operator configuring one or more provider records for the project
iWant: the provider adapter to validate every record's shape at boot and expose a fields-only surface to the flow controller
soThat: adding, removing, or swapping a provider is a config-record write with no code path change and no vendor-name branch

acceptanceCriteria.description: The provider adapter's boot-time validator enforces the provider-abstraction contract on every configured record and the flow controller reads only record fields on every step of the state machine. The two refusal ACs anchored under the sign-out and multi-provider stories (AC-10108-3, AC-10109-2) exercise this contract's refuse-fast behaviour at the concrete failure modes; this story's AC binds the shape-level property that every record must satisfy before either of those refuse-fast paths can even be reached.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project provider-config module carrying at least one record and the provider adapter loaded at boot per TAC-1102
acceptanceCriteria.when: the flow controller initiates any step of the authorisation-code + PKCE flow against the configured provider (mint redirect, exchange code, verify id_token, invoke userinfo, mint sign-out redirect)
acceptanceCriteria.then: every URL, credential, scope list, redirect target, and provider-kind determination the flow controller reads comes from the record's declared fields (`authorizeUrl`, `tokenUrl`, `userinfoUrl`, `issuer`, `jwksUri`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `scopes`, `redirectUri`, `providerKind`, `endSessionEndpoint`); a source-tree scan of the flow-controller module records zero string-literal branches keyed on a provider `id` value (no `provider.id === 'google'`, no vendor-name switch); a boot with a record missing any REQ-002-mandated field refuses with the stable-coded error class named on TAC-1102's responsibilities and no server process is left listening
